data.content_ref: inline:SRC_002 makes attack success depend on whether the attacker's warrant is newer than the defender's support chain's maximum timestamp. This breaks reinstatement as a derived property: a node A defeated by attacker B, where B is in turn defeated by C, need no longer be reinstated when C succeeds, because even after C's defeat the timestamp comparison between B and A's support chain can still decide A's status independently of B's acceptance. Thus a node's status can change solely due to timestamp comparisons, contradicting the required reinstatement guarantee. The target further admits timestamps may not be bounded by a polynomial of graph size, jeopardizing polynomial cost.
